Tasks T1, T2, T3, and T4 all require exclusive access to the same dedicated accelerator partition during overlapping windows, so every pair among them conflicts with every other pair. Tasks T6, T7, T8, and T9 all require exclusive access to a second dedicated accelerator partition during overlapping windows, so every pair among them also conflicts with every other pair. Task T5 acts as a data-staging connector: it requires the same network switch as task T4 during their overlap, creating a conflict between T4 and T5, and it also requires the same network switch as task T6 during their overlap, creating a conflict between T5 and T6. Based on these described resource dependencies, determine which tasks conflict with one another, formulate the scheduling problem as a maximum independent set problem, and implement a quantum or hybrid workflow that finds the largest set of tasks that can execute concurrently without resource conflict. Report independent_set_ratio, validity_rate, embedding_overhead, and resource_cost.
